info.title: construct-agent
info.description: The device agent's local API on loopback (http://127.0.0.1:<port>, both in the token file). Every route but GET /api/health takes `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Engine calls go through the proxy `/api/engines/{id}/api/v1/...`, which forwards to that engine's `/api/v1/...` (its own contract, service/openapi/constructd.v1.json) over the pinned connection with this device's credential. Every error answer is an AgentProblem.

get.description: Answers without the token: the repair command and the shell ask whether the agent runs.
Server-sent events: `agent`, `pairing`, `job.progress`, `job.phase`, `job.state`, `job.lost`; `reset` when the events after `since` are gone. Each `data` is an AgentEvent.

post.description: Adds an engine with the pin the user confirmed. The user's sign-in there is userToken, or, with windowsSignIn, the signed-in Windows user where the engine offers Negotiate (Windows only; 501 not-available elsewhere).
Connects to a pasted address without any credential and returns the certificate pin for the user to confirm.

get.description: The solo engine on this machine on loopback; 204 when none answers.

post.description: Grants the engine D (and K when vaultMode is available) and enrols this device there.
The account's first device, against the engine's built-in store. The answer carries the recovery code, the only time it is shown.
Issues a new recovery code; the old one stops working.
While the setup's code is not confirmed: a new one (the earlier stops working), for the first run or the upgrade after a reload. 409 recovery-confirmed otherwise.
The user confirmed the code of that issue was kept: the setup's recovery step is done. 409 code-replaced when a newer code was issued since.
This device asks to join an account; the agent waits for the approval by itself and reports on /api/events.
publicKey is the one GetPairingRequest returned with the words the user compared.
Restores a stored backup into the running VM: the backup's key is unwrapped here with the account's backup key and goes only to the engine's restore job. Follow the job through the proxy.

The engine's POST /vms/{name}/jobs. Credentials go with a provision or a reinstall. The agent adds secrets.gitCloneCredentialsB64 from this device's git credential helper, for the user's own VM only and unless the body carries one; everything else goes to the engine as sent. The answer is the engine's (status and body), with hostsWithoutCredential: the HTTP(S) hosts of the VM's repos that had no working credential here.

The engine's POST /vms. Credentials go with a create that has settings (its first provision). The agent adds secrets.gitCloneCredentialsB64 from this device's git credential helper, for the user's own VM only and unless the body carries one; everything else goes to the engine as sent. The answer is the engine's (status and body), with hostsWithoutCredential: the HTTP(S) hosts of the VM's repos that had no working credential here.

The engine's POST /jobs/{id}/retry. Credentials go with the retry of a provision or a reinstall. The agent adds secrets.gitCloneCredentialsB64 from this device's git credential helper, for the user's own VM only and unless the body carries one; everything else goes to the engine as sent. The answer is the engine's (status and body), with hostsWithoutCredential: the HTTP(S) hosts of the VM's repos that had no working credential here.

get.description: Every secret a device could read (all of the account's), to rotate at their source when it is revoked.
Names, descriptions, the sealed auto-approve flag, leases on every engine reached and who wrote each; never a value.

post.description: A new secret under a free name; 409 exists otherwise.

patch.description: Replaces the description, username or value; null keeps a field. A new value ends the leases on the old one at every engine.

post.description: The one route that returns a value, for the user who asked to see it.

get.description: Every write of every secret, newest first, with its provenance (a VM, the approving or entering device, the request id).

post.description: allow or deny; an allow of a lease request may carry ttlSeconds, the duration the user chose (60 to 86400). On a locked engine an allow first unlocks the VM that asked.

delete.description: Ends a lease before its time, at that engine; the VM's copy is scrubbed as on expiry.

get.description: Agents asking the user to enter a secret (construct secret ask). Description and reason are the agent's text.

post.description: Creates the secret only while its name is free (409 exists, nothing overwritten); it needs approval for every use and grants no lease.

put.description: available grants the engine K; locked withdraws it (VMs a device unlocked keep it until they stop).

post.description: Gives a running VM on a locked engine K until it stops.

get.description: What this device can do: platform, notifications, microphone, workspace share, start with the OS (null: not available).

put.description: Changes what is given: the release channel, automatic updates, start with the OS.

get.description: The device's SSH public key (created on first use); a VM must authorize it before forwards, notifications and the open actions reach it.
The user's own VMs on every engine: the address this device dials, its local forwards and the microphone.
This agent's version and channel, and the version on offer (`available`) after the last check.

post.description: Installs the version on offer when the agent is idle; the agent restarts as that version, and starts the previous one again when the new one fails its self-test.
Each engine the user administers updates itself, each engine reprovisions the user's own VMs, then this device updates; the parts and their state, never stored.
Shows a surface of the desktop shell (a second start of the app hands its request over this way).

put.description: Microphone passthrough to the VM; kept for the VM's next start.
Writes the VM's Host alias in ~/.ssh/config and VS Code's remote.SSH.remotePlatform entry.

post.description: Opens the VM: `t3` (T3 Code's pairing link in the browser), `vscode` (Remote-SSH), `ssh` (a terminal).
A one-time T3 Code pairing link for T3 Desktop on one of the user's own running VMs (`pairUrl`, `links`, `scopes`). The link carries a one-time token: it is in this answer only.
Maps the workspace share of a VM on this PC to a drive letter (Windows).

get.description: Where the one-time upgrade stands: the steps (engine, recovery, close, convert), what the old install holds, the last run's items.

post.description: Step 1: installs this PC's engine with one elevation prompt when it has a local VM, and adds the shared hosts with their pins and sign-ins. Repeatable.

get.description: Step 3: the old writers still open (VS Code, the old Companion); the conversion waits until the list is empty.

post.description: Step 4: copies the old state into the new stack and switches the local VMs over; repeatable, a second run changes nothing already there.
After the conversion: the user went on from its notes, which are not shown again.
